record.context_brief: Short-time existence with algebraic decay and hard potentials
record.original_question: Can one prove a short-time existence theory for the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and algebraically decaying initial data? The open case singled out in the paper is hard potentials gamma > 0 with initial data behaving like f_0 <= <v>^{-q}.

evidence.quote: As far as we are aware, there are no further short-time existence results for the inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation without cutoff explicitly covered in the literature. The case of initial data with algebraic decay rate (as in f0 . hvi−q ), with hard potentials (γ > 0) is not handled by any documented result. It is remarkable that even though the Boltzmann equation is one of the most studied problems in mathematical physics, such a basic question still remains unanswered.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation without angular cutoff
\[
\partial_t f + v\cdot\nabla_x f \;=\; Q(f,f), \qquad t>0,\ x\in\mathbb{T}^3\ (\text{or } \mathbb{R}^3),\ v\in\mathbb{R}^3,
\]
where the collision operator is
\[
Q(f,f)(v)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}\int_{\mathbb{S}^2} B(|v-v_*|,\cos\theta)\bigl(f(v')f(v_*')-f(v)f(v_*)\bigr)\,d\sigma\,dv_*,
\]
with post-collisional velocities $v'=\tfrac{v+v_*}{2}+\tfrac{|v-v_*|}{2}\sigma$, $v_*'=\tfrac{v+v_*}{2}-\tfrac{|v-v_*|}{2}\sigma$, and $\cos\theta=\sigma\cdot\tfrac{v-v_*}{|v-v_*|}$. Assume a non-cutoff hard-potential collision kernel
\[
B(|v-v_*|,\cos\theta)=|v-v_*|^{\gamma}\,b(\cos\theta), \qquad \gamma\in(0,1],
\]
where the angular cross section $b$ satisfies the standard non-integrable singularity
\[
b(\cos\theta)\sin\theta \;\sim\; \theta^{-1-2s}\quad\text{as }\theta\to 0^+,\qquad s\in(0,1).
\]
Let $\langle v\rangle = (1+|v|^2)^{1/2}$. Assume the initial datum $f_0:\mathbb{T}^3_x\times\mathbb{R}^3_v\to[0,\infty)$ is measurable and satisfies the polynomial (algebraic) decay bound
\[
0\le f_0(x,v)\le C\,\langle v\rangle^{-q}, \qquad (x,v)\in\mathbb{T}^3\times\mathbb{R}^3,
\]
for some $q>0$ sufficiently large (depending only on $\gamma$ and $s$), with no requirement of exponential (Gaussian or Maxwellian) decay in $v$.

Question: Prove that there exists $T>0$ and a (weak or classical) solution $f\ge 0$ to the Cauchy problem on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{T}^3\times\mathbb{R}^3$ with $f|_{t=0}=f_0$, satisfying a corresponding pointwise bound $f(t,x,v)\le C'\langle v\rangle^{-q'}$, uniformly on $[0,T]$. In other words, develop a short-time existence theory for the inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials ($\gamma>0$) and merely algebraically decaying initial data.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2026 preprint establishes local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to the spatially inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and polynomially decaying initial data, but conditional on pointwise bounds on the hydrodynamic quantities (mass, energy, entropy). Thus the problem has been partially solved, with conditional/local results available but no unconditional short-time existence theory yet documented in the fully general form.

status_evidence.title: Local well-posedness for the Boltzmann equation with hard potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Local-in-time existence and uniqueness of weak solutions for the spatially inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials and polynomially decaying initial data, conditional on pointwise bounds on mass, energy and entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a conditional local well-posedness result for the precise setting of the question (hard potentials, algebraic decay).

status_evidence.title: Local well-posedness of the Boltzmann equation with polynomially decaying initial data
status_evidence.snippet: Short-time existence for the spatially inhomogeneous non-cutoff Boltzmann equation with polynomially decaying initial data in a mixed L^2/L^infty Sobolev framework.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier short-time existence results in similar polynomial-decay frameworks, primarily for moderate/soft regimes.

status_evidence.title: Local Well-Posedness for the Boltzmann Equation with Very Soft Potential and Polynomially Decaying Initial Data
status_evidence.snippet: Local well-posedness for very soft potentials with polynomially decaying data.
status_evidence.claim: Companion result handling soft potentials, illustrating gap that hard potential case required separate treatment.
